To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CBT delivered using an automated media rich internet based course is effective in improving sleep and associated daytime function in adults with insomnia disorder, and that the improvements were maintained during follow up, and that the course was well received by participants.

CBT delivered using an animated virtual therapist, with automated email and web based support is effective in improving both sleep and daytime functioning, in adults with insomnia disorder and is more effective than a placebo.
CBT delivered using an automated media rich virtual therapist and a web based community is effective in improving sleep and daytime functioning of adults diagnosed with insomnia disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and evaluating the effectiveness of a new approach to the delivery of cognitive behavioral therapy ( CBT) for chronic insomnia.
understanding how the brain works in the context of sleep and sleep disorders.
developing and testing new methods of delivering cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) using the Internet and other new technologies.
